analysis.answer: Under current law, assault is punishable by up to one year in jail. The proposed measure elevates the crime specifically for assaults on on-duty hospital workers, making it a felony punishable by up to three years in prison.

Direct costs will increase for the state prison system due to the longer sentences and the shift from jail (typically county-funded) to prison (state-funded). Opportunity costs include state funds that could have been spent on other programs.
Hospital workers benefit from the specific legal protection. State taxpayers bear the increased costs of housing inmates in state prisons for longer terms.
Prosecutors may use the threat of a felony conviction and a three-year prison sentence to negotiate plea deals. Hospital workers may feel their safety is taken more seriously by the legal system.

The text addresses the problem of workplace violence against healthcare workers. The mechanism increases the criminal penalty for such assaults, which is intended to punish offenders more severely and deter future violence, though the deterrence effect of longer sentences is debated.

items.text: Specific workplace protections and harsher penalties for assaulting on-duty hospital workers.

give_up.empty_reason: The text does not reduce any worker protections or decrease any penalties.

items.text: Increases the maximum sentence for assaulting an on-duty hospital worker to three years in prison and classifies the offense as a felony.
